review_cost.rationale: I'd approve after one round of small, mechanical changes; nothing requires rearchitecting. All nits are localized with obvious fixes.

findings.issue: pokemonCard indexes typeLabels as a plain object (typeLabels[t.name]) but app.js:72 passes the Map returned by typeEnglishByName() (api.js), so the lookup is always undefined and silently masked by the humanize() fallback — it only renders correctly because every type slug happens to humanize to its English name.
findings.suggestion: Pick one shape: have typeEnglishByName return a plain object, or call typeLabels.get(t.name) in the component; consider making the fallback loud (throw or log) so the mismatch can't hide.

findings.issue: Debounced active search without hx-sync: per htmx docs, typing again while a request is in flight starts a parallel request, and responses can swap into #results out of order, briefly showing stale results for the typed query.
findings.suggestion: Add hx-sync="this:replace" to the form (or #q) as the htmx active-search example shows, so the last request wins.

findings.issue: onError returns bare c.text('Internal Server Error', 500) — breaks the page chrome on a full-page load and injects raw text into the htmx swap on fragment requests.
findings.suggestion: Return a styled 500 page (renderPage with the layout) and a small inline error fragment when HX-Request is set.

findings.issue: One failing move fetch (non-404 API error) inside mapLimit rejects the whole Pokémon page request with a 500.
findings.suggestion: Catch per-item in the move fetch (app.js:139-141) and degrade to humanized-name rows like the rec-missing path already does.

findings.issue: Static assets served by a hand-enumerated loop of four exact paths, so any new file under public/ needs a route edit; the framework feature is a single wildcard serveStatic.
findings.suggestion: Replace with one app.use('*', serveStatic({ root: './public' })) (or app.use('/vendor/*', ...) plus explicit entries) so new assets are picked up automatically.

findings.issue: renderPage's second parameter is named h1 but the home route (app.js:79) passes 'Pokédex' — the desired document title — while the page's real h1 is 'Pokémon'; pageTitle special-cases 'Pokédex' to make it work.
findings.suggestion: Pass the title text explicitly (renderPage(c, { title, main })) or let renderPage take the real h1 and a separate homeTitle override, and name things accordingly.

findings.issue: typeLabels is converted via Object.fromEntries for typePage but passed as a Map to pokemonCard, so two different access idioms (t.name vs .get) coexist for the same lookup table — this is what allowed the components.js:21 mismatch to slip through.
findings.suggestion: Standardise on one typeLabels shape across all view call sites.

findings.issue: movesSection hand-builds <section id="moves" aria-labelledby="moves-heading"> although components.js:31 already exports a section() helper that takes an optional id and produces exactly this markup.
findings.suggestion: Reuse section('moves', 'Moves', content, 'moves') to remove the duplicate pattern.

findings.issue: typeBadge can be called with an empty name/label (move record missing its type in app.js:142-143), producing a link to /types/ with no accessible name.
findings.suggestion: Render MISSING (—) when name or label is empty instead of an empty badge link.

findings.issue: A view component imports API_BASE from the data layer to build sprite URLs, coupling rendering to the API config module.
findings.suggestion: Pass resolved sprite URLs from the route (the data layer already knows the base URL), keeping views free of server config.

summary: A clean, well-organised Hono + htmx app on the current stable framework: idiomatic hono/html rendering, proper htmx fragment branching, progressive enhancement, and a tidy data/views separation. The main issues are small but real: a Map-vs-object lookup mismatch masked by a lucky fallback, a documented htmx request race without hx-sync, and a couple of error-path and consistency nits. I'd merge after one round of minor, mechanical fixes.
